TEST 1
CAN THE UTILITY PAY?
FACT
WEAK COLLECTION
↓
PAYMENT RISK
↓
STATE GUARANTEE CALLED
↓
THE TREASURY PAYS
DECISION
THE QUESTION
Can the utility actually pay?
THE EVIDENCE
Collection: 70 of every 100 billed
Needed for costs and IPPs: 95
Some suppliers already paid late
THE DECISION
Don't sign until payment capacity is demonstrated.
The strongest guarantee is a utility that can pay.
TEST 2
CAN THE GRID ABSORB THE POWER?
FACT
Plant: 100 MW
FACT
Grid today: 60 MW
RED TEAM
40 MW
paid, never used.
DECISION
THE QUESTION
Can the grid absorb the contracted electricity?
THE EVIDENCE
Grid can absorb 60 of 100 MW
Line upgrade not financed
Take or pay: capacity paid whether dispatched or not
THE DECISION
Phase the plant with the grid. Don't pay for power you cannot use.
Take or pay is not bad in itself. Signed before the grid is ready, it bites.
TEST 3
WHO CARRIES THE RISK?
Lenders price risk.
When the State carries it,
the deal looks cheap.
The cost is simply hidden elsewhere.
FACT
PPA tariff
10 US cents per kWh
FACT
Year 1: $1 = 600 KVF
→ 60 KVF per kWh
FACT
Year 5: $1 = 800 KVF
→ 80 KVF per kWh
Same dollar tariff.
One third more
in local money.
RED TEAM
WHO CARRIES
THE FX RISK?
Here: the utility.
Behind it: the Treasury.
TEST 4
CAN THE PUBLIC SECTOR
LIVE WITH THE DEAL?
DECISION
THE QUESTION
What is the maximum, and the expected, fiscal exposure?
THE EVIDENCE
State guarantee with no ceiling
Take-or-pay commitments
Currency risk
Utility arrears
THE DECISION
Identify, measure and disclose every contingent liability before signing, not after.
STOP
You are the Director of Public Debt.
The lender says the loan is protected.
Protected by a State guarantee.
The guarantee has no ceiling.
It is not in the budget.
Would you issue it?
AYes, as requested
BYes, with a ceiling and a risk register
CNot yet

What could make this deal fail?
1The offtaker cannot pay
2The grid cannot absorb the power
3The government carries hidden obligations
Don't ask whether the project is attractive.
Ask what could break it.
THE SIGNING TEST
SHOULD WE SIGN?
1BANKABLELenders can finance it.✓
2AFFORDABLEThe utility and consumers can carry the cost.?
3EXECUTABLEThe grid and institutions can deliver it.?
4SUSTAINABLEPublic obligations remain manageable.?
BANKABLE ≠ SUSTAINABLE
BANKABLE IS NOT ENOUGH.
BEFORE YOU SIGN
01Can the utility actually pay?
02What exactly does the PPA require us to pay?
03Can the grid absorb the contracted electricity?
04Who carries the currency risk?
05What happens if the project fails or the contract terminates?
If you cannot answer these questions, you are not ready to sign.
BANKABLE IS NOT ENOUGH.
Before you sign, test the deal.
Bankability is the beginning. Not the end.
